headline: 4 goals for USA: USA rout Paraguay 4-1 in World Cup opener
summary: Folarin Balogun's brace and a dream start for the hosts as they secure a dominant victory in their first home-soil match in 32 years.
details: The United States launched their World Cup campaign with a commanding 4-1 victory over Paraguay in their Group D opener on Friday in Inglewood, California.
The hosts dominated the first half, securing a 3-0 lead by the break. The scoring opened in the seventh minute with an own goal by Paraguay's Damian Bobadilla.
Folarin Balogun then took center stage, scoring two goals in the 31st minute and during first-half stoppage time to further solidify the lead.
Paraguay managed to pull one back in the 73rd minute through Mauricio, but the US capped the match with a brilliant strike from Gio Reyna deep in second-half stoppage time.
The match marked a significant milestone as the US played a World Cup match on home soil for the first time in 32 years.
Key performances included Christian Pulisic, who provided critical build-up play, and the return of defender Chris Richards from injury.
Goalkeeper Matt Freese made his first World Cup appearance, starting over Matt Turner.
The US will next face Australia in Seattle on June 19, while Paraguay will play Turkey in Santa Clara, California.
caption:
A dream start for the hosts! 🇺🇸

USA crushes Paraguay 4-1 in their first home World Cup match in 32 years.

The United States launched their World Cup campaign with a commanding 4-1 victory over Paraguay in their Group D opener on Friday in Inglewood, California.

The hosts dominated the first half, securing a 3-0 lead by the break. The scoring opened in the seventh minute with an own goal by Paraguay's Damian Bobadilla.

Folarin Balogun then took center stage, scoring two goals in the 31st minute and during first-half stoppage time to further solidify the lead.

Paraguay managed to pull one back in the 73rd minute through Mauricio, but the US capped the match with a brilliant strike from Gio Reyna deep in second-half stoppage time.

The match marked a significant milestone as the US played a World Cup match on home soil for the first time in 32 years.

Key performances included Christian Pulisic, who provided critical build-up play, and the return of defender Chris Richards from injury.

Goalkeeper Matt Freese made his first World Cup appearance, starting over Matt Turner.

The US will next face Australia in Seattle on June 19, while Paraguay will play Turkey in Santa Clara, California.

headline_marked: Dhaka sent [[13 letters to Delhi to stop 'push-ins']]
headline: Dhaka sent 13 letters to Delhi to stop 'push-ins'
summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid says BGB is resisting attempts to push illegal migrants into Bangladesh from India.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid revealed that Bangladesh's Foreign Ministry has already sent 13 letters to Delhi demanding an end to 'push-ins' from India.
Speaking at a reception by the Saltha Upazila Press Club in Faridpur, she stated that the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) is currently in a difficult position while resisting these attempts.

The Minister emphasized that there are clear policies and mechanisms for the return of illegal citizens between any two countries, and she expressed hope that the Indian government would follow these established protocols.
She clarified that if any Bangladeshis are staying illegally in India, they should be returned through diplomatic channels and legal paths, and the same applies to illegal Indians in Bangladesh.
Obaid urged the Indian government to refrain from pushing people across the border under the cover of darkness, asserting that Bangladesh will continue to resolve the issue through diplomacy.

During the event, she also addressed the role of journalism, noting that while social media is becoming influential, it is often used to spread misinformation and AI-generated fake news against political opponents.
caption:
13 letters sent to Delhi. Bangladesh is demanding an end to illegal 'push-ins' at the border.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid revealed that Bangladesh's Foreign Ministry has already sent 13 letters to Delhi demanding an end to 'push-ins' from India.

Speaking at a reception by the Saltha Upazila Press Club in Faridpur, she stated that the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) is currently in a difficult position while resisting these attempts.

The Minister emphasized that there are clear policies and mechanisms for the return of illegal citizens between any two countries, and she expressed hope that the Indian government would follow these established protocols.

She clarified that if any Bangladeshis are staying illegally in India, they should be returned through diplomatic channels and legal paths, and the same applies to illegal Indians in Bangladesh.

Obaid urged the Indian government to refrain from pushing people across the border under the cover of darkness, asserting that Bangladesh will continue to resolve the issue through diplomacy.

During the event, she also addressed the role of journalism, noting that while social media is becoming influential, it is often used to spread misinformation and AI-generated fake news against political opponents.
